ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (79) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

Chekhov's story as Tolstoy printed it, translated closely from this Russian text. «Фельдшер» (fel'dsher) is 'doctor's assistant', «фельдшерица» (fel'dsheritsa, a woman feldsher) 'the woman assistant', and «сиделка» (sidelka) 'nurse'; the mother's «батюшка» (batyushka, literally 'little father') is 'sir' each time, so that the doctor's mockery of the word carries. Pashka's two night cries «Ма-а-ма» and «Ма-амка» (mamka, 'mammy') are kept distinct, and the doctor's «Ну и дурак» ('Well, what a fool') and «Бить ... да некому» ('beaten, but there's no one to do it') repeat at the end as in the source.
Source observation: [50] «хотел сделать то же самое но подумал»: the comma before «но» ('but') is missing; translated with the evident sense.
